help.lines: Grow your kingdom from a single city. Every city splits its gold between five budgets: ARMY trains the selected unit, TOWERS builds towers and walls, WORKSHOPS builds workshops, LAND cleans pollution, irrigates and grows the population, LEARNING funds research.
Select your Settlers in the garrison, press March and click a site inside the dashed supply circles. Settlers found a city when they arrive; better settler camps settle harsh lands.

Learning: choose one subject per field. Agriculture opens harsh lands and irrigation, Roads supply range, mounts and waygates, Masonry cheaper workshops and armour, Scholarship guild workshops and veterans, Smithing and Fortification everything for war. Higher levels make gear cheaper and lighter.
Army: design up to six unit types from sizes, weapons, veterans, shields, armour, mounts and gear. Replacing or disbanding a unit type disbands its units.
To conquer a city, defeat its army and towers, then send levies from a nearby city. Armies holding an enemy city besiege it (see Cities to turn this off).

Battles: when your armies or cities meet an enemy, the battle is fought on a field divided in squares. Units act in order of initiative: click a lit square to march, an enemy in a red frame to attack. Javelins take turns to arrive and can be dodged; rocks block volleys. Spells like the Freezing Spell have their own button. Let your captains fight if you prefer.
Mists bring down walls and halve the pace. Waygates between your cities move armies in one turn. A dragon guards Orion: slaying it reveals its ancient library.

Kingdoms: you meet other kingdoms when your cities come within supply range of theirs. Send an envoy to propose pacts, alliances, peace and trade routes, to threaten, to offer tribute or to exchange knowledge. Their mood and how much they trust you decide the answer; allies share supply range and never fight.

Spies: give a budget per kingdom, then send them to steal secrets or to burn workshops, bring down towers or stir up revolt. Watchmen catch enemy spies. Taxes (Cities) fill the treasury, which you can send to any city.
Fate strikes: plagues, volcanoes, floods, bandits, giants and wyrms, revolts. Send levies to a rebel city to restore order.

Win by defeating every rival kingdom, or by being crowned High King by two thirds of the votes of the Great Council, which gathers every 25 years once two thirds of the land is settled. Refusing its verdict means war against everyone.
